text:
mia: Quick heads-up — we need to unify the routing fields in telemetry. Current event has `destination` as a freeform string but our new routing model needs `routing.policy` (enum: direct|fallback|split) + `routing.target` (string). This will change schema for console analytics and quota lookups. Planning a migration next Wed during the low-traffic window. Thoughts?

nate: sounds necessary. do we have a backward-compat plan? dashboards + alerts will break if we suddenly stop emitting `destination`.

anika: agree. can we emit both fields for a transitional period? i.e., keep `destination` and add `routing.*` for 30 days, then backfill history and drop `destination` after validation.

harry: emitting both is easiest for producers, but storage/schema costs bump. how big is the message/row increase? our analytics cluster charges by storage/retention.

mia: estimated +8% storage for events table if we keep both for 30d. cost is acceptable vs user facing breakage. we should also add a feature-flagged view in clickhouse/postgres to map old -> new.

jyoti: suggestion: instead of immediate drop, create a DB view `events_v2` that exposes `routing.policy` derived from `destination` when `routing.policy` is NULL. then update console queries to use the view. that avoids backfilling raw rows immediately.

nate: +1 to the view approach. also need to update the embed/console quota calc job — it queries `destination` today. i'll add a migration ticket to update it to `routing.policy` and fall back to `destination` if missing.

anika: for backfill, we can run a streaming job to populate `routing.*` for historical rows. propose: (1) emit both for 30d, (2) deploy view and update console to read the view, (3) run backfill over 7 days indexed by partition, (4) flip producers to only emit `routing.*`, (5) drop `destination` after another 7d monitoring window.

harry: how about dashboards with group-by on routing — we need to ensure enum values are stable. will producers send unknown strings in `destination` that don't map to enum?

mia: good point. plan to add a normalization table and mapping function in the view. unknowns map to `direct` or `unknown` depending on pattern, and we log exceptions to telemetry.

deploy-bot: migration-job-1789012345 scheduled: staging run Fri 09:00 UTC, prod canary Mon 02:00 UTC if staging looks good.

jyoti: ops question — any reindexing on big tables? backfill may scan 500M rows. need throttling and run during off-peak partitions. i'll write a backfill runbook with safe throttles and retries.

nate: add a short-lived feature-flag for the console route that flips query to use `events_v2` per workspace. canary on 5% of orgs for 48h. roll forward if no anomalies in cost/latency and top routes graph.

anika: tests: unit mappers, integration for console query latency, and an E2E where producers emit only `routing.*` and we verify dashboards show identical numbers (within 0.5%) before dropping `destination`.

mia: i'll draft the runbook: schema DDL, view SQL, backfill job spec, canary checklist, rollback steps. will post RFC by EOD. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

harry: one last note — quota enforcement service uses `destination` tag for per-route quotas. need to ensure it reads the normalized field or we risk misbilling. put that on the migration checklist.

nate: capturing that — i'll own quota service change and test with the canary orgs.

mia: perfect. i'll set the migration PR and link deploy-bot job. everyone put any blockers in the RFC comments.
